analysis.title: US Inflation Monitor: October 2026: A Third Month of Worse Inflation News
key_insights: Core CPI rose 0.30% m/m in October and headline CPI rose 0.35% m/m. From the CPI and PPI details, GS estimates core PCE rose 0.29% m/m and 3.24% y/y, and headline PCE rose 0.32% m/m and 3.83% y/y.
GS core goods PCE estimate is +0.36% m/m in October (vs +0.20% in September, 2.4% y/y). Core services PCE is estimated at +0.28% (vs +0.36% in September, 3.5% y/y).

Core inflation trend measures accelerated on a monthly basis in September and October. Examples are Atlanta Fed core sticky CPI at 0.38%, Cleveland Fed 16% trimmed mean at 0.37% and Core CPI at 0.30%, against GS trimmed core at 0.21%.

Breadth of high inflation is above the 1990-2019 average but well below the 2022 pandemic peak. On a 0 to 10 scale the share of PCE categories above 3% is 2 with tariffs (1 without) and the share above 6% is 2. The share above 3% rose after the Iran war started and has edged lower on net in recent months.

Iran war energy shock: GS puts the effect on y/y core PCE at 0.5pp so far, peaking at 0.6pp and fading to 0.1pp by end-2027. GS thinks the largest effects on monthly inflation are behind us. Commodity passthrough still adds about 3bp per month to core PCE in the coming months.

Oil has fallen since the US midterm elections but averages $96/barrel in November vs $69 before the war. GS oil strategists see $100/barrel at year-end 2026 and $78 at end-2027. Gasoline is forecast at $4.32/gallon and diesel at $6.04/gallon at year-end.

AI demand is raising prices of electronic inputs. The PPI for electronic components rose 4% m/m in October, and September import prices rose 4% for computer peripherals and parts and 7% for semiconductors. Memory prices have risen around 250-300% Q4/Q4 in 2026.

GS estimates software and accessories prices rose 16% y/y in October, adding 0.20pp to y/y core PCE. Consumer electronics categories add another 0.15pp. The CPI effect is much smaller because the component has a smaller weight in CPI than in PCE.

GS estimates AI price pressures add 0.45pp to core PCE inflation now, about half of it genuine rather than mismeasurement. The effect is seen peaking at 0.55pp at end-2026 and falling to 0.15pp by end-2027. Data center electricity demand adds 0.1pp to headline PCE in 2026Q4.

GS equity analysts expect memory price growth to slow to 5-10% in 2027 (Q4/Q4), slightly below consensus of 10-15%. This underlies the forecast that computers (-11%), phone services (-1%), video games (9%) and consoles (7%) inflation slows by end-2027.

Tariffs add 0.4pp to y/y core PCE inflation now (peak 0.8pp in April), falling to 0.3pp at end-2026 and below 0.1pp at end-2027. GS expects Democratic efforts to reverse some tariffs to have limited effect and expects new Trump tariff increases after the election that raise the effective tariff rate by a little under 2pp.
Shelter: the best alternative measures of new lease rent growth rose to 2.2% y/y in September from 1.9% in August. Single-family rent growth rose to 1.8% from 1.6%.

Inflation expectations retraced part of the post-war jump. UMich 1-year fell 0.4pp to 4.3% and 5-10 year fell 0.1pp to 3.4%. NY Fed 1-year was unchanged at 3.9% and 5-year unchanged at 3.0%. Swap-implied 2027 CPI is unchanged at 2.2% and 2028 fell 0.1pp to 2.4%.
GS forecasts core PCE of 3.2% in December 2026 and 2.4% in December 2027, and core CPI of 2.9% in December 2026 and 2.2% in December 2027, as tariff, energy and AI effects fade.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Core CPI rose 0.30% in October. Trend measures of monthly core inflation accelerated in September and October.
Headline CPI rose 0.35% m/m in October.

macro_indicators.indicator: Core PCE m/m and y/y (GS estimate)
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS estimate built from the October CPI and PPI details ahead of the PCE release. Core PCE is running above 3% y/y.

macro_indicators.indicator: Headline PCE m/m and y/y (GS estimate)
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS estimate ahead of the PCE release.
Core goods accelerates from +0.20% in September, partly on prescription drug prices and the lower weight of used cars in PCE.
Core services slows from +0.36% in September.
Inflation is forecast to fall as tariff, energy shock and AI price effects fade.
Core CPI is forecast to converge to roughly 2% by end-2027.
Oil is expected to stay elevated through year-end before declining in 2027.
Oil has fallen since the US midterm elections but remains well above pre-war levels.
Short-term household expectations declined but remain high.

macro_indicators.indicator: New lease rent growth, alternative measures
macro_indicators.interpretation: New lease rent growth picked up, which is a leading indicator for shelter inflation.

risk_factors: Near-term effects of the war and AI demand on prices remain uncertain
Further memory price increases beyond GS forecasts would extend AI-related pressure on core PCE
Oil and refined product prices depend on 2027 Gulf supply, with upside and downside scenarios 2.5 mb/d either side of the 2025 average
New tariff increases after the election could raise the effective tariff rate by a little under 2pp
charts_described: Exhibit 5 shows the share of 6m annualized core PCE inflation by range, with the 1990-2019 average shares at 12%, 24% and 36% for the >6%, 4-6% and 3-4% bands per the exhibit labels.

Exhibit 14 shows GS estimates that commodity prices will add 3bp per month to core PCE in the coming months, with the y/y impact peaking at 0.6pp early next year before declining to 0.1pp by end-2027.
Exhibit 18 shows AI price pressures on core PCE rising from 45bp today to 55bp at end-2026 before falling to 15bp by end-2027.
geopolitical: Iran war energy shock still feeding refined product and commodity prices, with Gulf supply the main variable in GS oil scenarios
US midterm elections: newly elected Democrats say they would seek to reverse some tariffs, GS expects limited effect
GS expects new Trump tariff increases after the election that raise the effective tariff rate by a little under 2pp

theme_stances.key_argument: The largest effects on monthly inflation from energy, AI and tariffs are behind us, and core PCE falls to 2.4% by end-2027.
theme_stances.evidence: largest effects on monthly inflation are likely behind us
